mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__drou.mechanism: In a national census of post-tsunami mangrove planting sites in Sri Lanka, seedlings and propagules planted in the higher intertidal zone of the dry and arid zones suffered from drought and high irradiance [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_2].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__drou.conditionality: This is a single observational source; it describes stress at poorly sited plantings rather than measuring how much drought reduced survival, and it points to planting position along the tidal gradient as the controlling factor.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__extr.mechanism: Compilers judge mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with local rainstorms and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping well with local thunderstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1442_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4300_2019_local_thunderstorm].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__extr.conditionality: Both units are practitioner judgements of good coping, with no observed damage behind the threat class.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__floo.mechanism: Flooding was among the stress factors observed at all planted mangrove sites in a national census in Sri Lanka, alongside drought, smothering, high irradiance, browsing and cattle trampling [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_3]. In Vietnam's Bac Lieu province mangrove replanting was less successful, mostly because of heavy storms and flooding and poor planting techniques [ev_frmg_vnppar_5].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__floo.conditionality: Compilers rate mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with river floods, mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping well with storm surge and mangrove buffers in the Philippines as coping very well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1442_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_4300_2019_storm_surge_coastal_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_578_2016_storm_surge_coastal_flood], so these ratings are practitioner judgements of slight threat; the Sri Lankan observation does not separate flooding from the other stresses. The Bac Lieu account, relayed by an independent evaluation, likewise does not separate flooding from storms and poor planting technique, and it concerns newly planted stands that failed to establish rather than an established forest [ev_frmg_vnppar_5]. The threat falls on the establishment window and on siting.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__sedi.mechanism: Rapid sedimentation and excess leaf litter can cause delayed mortality of mangrove trees by smothering the above-ground aerial roots [ev_establishment_survival_gijsman21_1].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__sedi.conditionality: The evidence is a single review statement on existing mangrove forests with no magnitude; whether planted or regenerating stands are affected the same way is not tested here.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__wate.mechanism: In Sri Lanka, mangrove seedlings and propagules planted in the low intertidal zone of the wet zone were exposed to long-term submergence due to heavy rains [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_1].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__wate.conditionality: This is a single observational source that does not quantify the resulting losses; the exposure is linked to the planting position along the tidal gradient, a siting error rather than a property of the practice.

mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__wind.mechanism: Mangrove tree damage rises rapidly once tropical-cyclone winds exceed 130 km/h, and extreme events with very high water levels and wind speeds may severely damage or destroy mangrove areas, leaving them less able to reduce surge [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1]. In Florida the 2005 Hurricane Wilma was estimated to have initially destroyed 1250 ha of mangroves, and frequent hurricanes have changed some mangrove stands to mudflats [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. In Vietnam's Bac Lieu province mangrove replanting was less successful, mostly because of heavy storms and flooding and poor planting techniques, and project staff told the evaluation mission that a severe storm arriving before the roots could take a firm hold in the sand would take out enough seedlings to require yet another replanting [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7].
mangrove_restoration__asset_threat__wind.conditionality: Compilers judge mangrove regeneration in Senegal as coping well with local windstorms and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh as coping moderately with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1442_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4300_2019_tropical_storm]. The review units, including the Florida loss estimate, are cited findings for existing mangrove forests, not measurements on restored stands [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_establishment_survival_mcivor12_1, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. The Vietnam accounts are the only ones about planted stands; they are evaluator and project-staff reports rather than measurements, and the Bac Lieu losses mix storms, flooding and poor planting technique [ev_frmg_vnppar_6, ev_frmg_vnppar_7]. The exposure is sharpest before the roots take hold, so the threat to an investment sits in the establishment years.

mangrove_restoration__biodiversity_prior.mechanism: In a global meta-analysis of mostly planted mangrove restoration, restored mangroves exhibit higher levels of crab production and diversity than degraded mangroves (RR′ = 0.80, 95% CIs = 0.64 to 0.97) [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_1]. A WOCAT mangrove afforestation sheet from Bangladesh reports that the plantation site supports habitats for birds and crabs and develops suitable habitats for wildlife and fish [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4300_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4300_2019_habitat_diversity]. In Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta an independent evaluation relays that forest cover in the protection zones increased from around 50 percent in 2000 to 96 percent in 2007 as a result of the project, and that the zones around mangrove roots protected from the violence of the sea created breeding grounds for fish and shellfish, with sea crabs and shellfish re-appearing in some places and increasing in others [ev_frmg_vnppar_3, ev_frmg_vnppar_4].
mangrove_restoration__biodiversity_prior.conditionality: The same meta-analysis found no major difference in crab or fish production and diversity between restored mangroves and unvegetated tidal flats, and its metric merges production with diversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_su21_2], so the gain depends on the comparison: it holds against degraded mangrove, not against the open tidal flat. The Bangladesh entries are compiler ratings, not measurements. The Vietnam cover figure is before-and-after project data with no counterfactual, which stakeholders described as only partly attributable to the project; it includes casuarina windbreak planting and protection of existing forest, and it is cover rather than a count of species [ev_frmg_vnppar_3]. The return of crabs and shellfish is an anecdotal observation, and it came with protection contracts given to smallholders as well as the replanting [ev_frmg_vnppar_4].

mangrove_restoration__carbon_sequestrati.mechanism: Planted mangroves take up CO2 rapidly as the trees grow: a global review of forest landscape restoration finds mangrove tree restoration the second most efficient type at removing CO2, at up to 23.1 t CO2 per hectare per year in the first 20 years and 10.5 over the following 40 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_4]. A mangrove meta-analysis also finds higher carbon sequestration in restored mangroves than in unvegetated tidal flats (RR′ = 0.64, 95% CIs = 0.35 to 0.94) [ev_carbon_sequestration_su21_1]. In Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta forest cover in the protection zones increased from around 50 percent in 2000 to 96 percent in 2007 as a result of the project, which enters here as cover rather than a carbon stock [ev_frmg_vnppar_3].
mangrove_restoration__carbon_sequestrati.conditionality: The removal-rate review covers active planting only, and its text and table give slightly different later-period rates [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_4]; the meta-analysis reports publication bias for carbon sequestration against tidal flats [ev_carbon_sequestration_su21_1]. The Bangladesh WOCAT sheet contributes only a compiler rating of increased below-ground soil organic matter, a component proxy for sequestration [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4300_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. The Vietnam cover figure is project before-and-after data with no counterfactual, only partly attributable to the project according to stakeholders, and it mixes replanting with casuarina windbreaks and protection of existing forest [ev_frmg_vnppar_3]. The rates are those of stands that established; a planting that washes out sequesters nothing.

mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.mechanism: These are per-hectare costs of establishing mangroves, mostly by planting. Compiler-entered establishment costs are 427.38 USD/ha on a WOCAT sheet from Bangladesh and 150.00 USD/ha from the Philippines [ev_project_cost_wocat_4300_2019_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_578_2016_establishment]. Cited reforestation costs are US$946/ha in Thailand, US$211/ha for community-supported reforestation in the Philippines and US$990.96/ha in Vietnam [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_3, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_4, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_5]; a community project in northern Viet Nam put the present-value cost to create one hectare of mangrove at 843 US dollars [ev_project_cost_ifrc11_1]. A global meta-analysis gives a median total restoration cost of 1,097.16 USD/ha within a range of 23.22 to 371,326.75 USD/ha [ev_project_cost_su21_1], a global cost-carbon study uses an average of US$4368 per hectare [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_3], and a World Bank study models a national mean of 7,700 USD/ha for Bangladesh [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].
mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.conditionality: The figures rest on different cost bases. The Mexican value, US$94.68/ha, was set by budget availability under a subsidy programme rather than being a full cost, and the authors argue it was insufficient for success [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_1]; the Philippine community-supported figure excludes preliminary and maintenance activities, which raise it to US$1,156.52/ha [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_5]; several cited figures state no price year; and the meta-analysis range runs from direct propagule dibbing at the low end to very costly projects [ev_project_cost_su21_1]. WOCAT costs are compiler entries converted from local currency, and the World Bank figure is a value transfer from a cost function rather than an observed project cost [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].

mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.mechanism: In lower-middle-income settings the costs run from US$211/ha for community-supported mangrove reforestation in the Philippines and a compiler-entered 427.38 USD/ha for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh, through US$990.96/ha cited for reforestation in Vietnam, to a modelled national mean of 7,700 USD/ha for mangrove restoration in Bangladesh [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_4, ev_project_cost_wocat_4300_2019_establishment, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_5, ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].
mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.conditionality: The Philippine figure excludes preliminary and maintenance activities, which raise it to US$1,156.52/ha [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_5], so figures that omit them understate full cost. The Vietnam value is a citation of the IFRC evaluation with no stated price year, the Bangladesh WOCAT value is a compiler entry converted from local currency, and the 7,700 USD/ha mean is a modelled value transfer from grey literature, far above the observed community-supported planting costs [ev_project_cost_wbmang25_1].

mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the reported costs are US$946/ha cited for mangrove reforestation in Thailand, 843 US dollars at present value to create one hectare of mangrove in a community project in northern Viet Nam, a compiler-entered 150.00 USD/ha for mangrove buffers in the Philippines, and US$94.68/ha allocated per hectare in Tabasco, Mexico [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_3, ev_project_cost_ifrc11_1, ev_project_cost_wocat_578_2016_establishment, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_1].
mangrove_restoration__cost_per_hectare_r.conditionality: The lowest value is not a full cost: the Mexican amount was determined according to budget availability and the authors argue it was insufficient for success [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_1]. The Viet Nam figure is a present value from an implementer-commissioned evaluation, the Thai figure is a citation with no stated price year, and the Philippine figure is a compiler entry converted from local currency [ev_project_cost_ifrc11_1, ev_project_cost_hernmel17_3, ev_project_cost_wocat_578_2016_establishment].

mangrove_restoration__cost_per_tco2e_avo.mechanism: A global spatial cost-carbon model estimates the break-even carbon price at which carbon payments would cover land opportunity and restoration costs, and finds that carbon prices between 4.5 and 18.0 US$ per tCO2 could support the restoration of 90% of deforested mangroves [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_1].
mangrove_restoration__cost_per_tco2e_avo.conditionality: This is a modelled break-even price from a single global study with no country context, not an observed project cost per tonne; it depends on the assumed opportunity and restoration costs and on the share of carbon credited, and it assumes the restored stands establish.

mangrove_restoration__cost_reduction.mechanism: The only unit is a cited project in Tabasco, Mexico, where 50 ha of black mangrove were reforested successfully at a full per-hectare cost covering sanitation, dredging, soil conservation works, ridge restoration, staff training, plant production, transplanting and monitoring [ev_project_cost_hernmel17_2].
mangrove_restoration__cost_reduction.conditionality: It is a single cited project report from an upper-middle-income setting that shows what successful restoration costs when preparatory and follow-up work are included, rather than a measured saving; the source's printed value could not be used as a magnitude.

mangrove_restoration__flood__all.mechanism: Compilers for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and mangrove buffers in the Philippines rate flood impacts as decreased, the Bangladesh compiler only slightly [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts]. Of the mangrove restoration projects reviewed globally, 50% state that the habitat provides improved protection from storm events [ev_frmg_nara16_5], and a second-hand reading of an economic model for coastal districts of northern Vietnam reports that restoration scenarios have even higher cost-benefit ratios when the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is included [ev_frmg_erw09_2].
mangrove_restoration__flood__all.conditionality: No unit here measures how far a planted stand lowers flood water or waves. The WOCAT entries are compiler ratings; the 50% counts projects that report a benefit, self-reported rather than measured; and the Vietnam dike-cost result is a model read second-hand from the original study, which the citing author does not describe further [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The protection these units describe falls on the coast and the sea dike behind the stand - avoided storm damage and avoided dike maintenance that accrue to society at large, not income for the household that plants or tends the mangroves [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].

mangrove_restoration__flood__all__income.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the row holds two units: the compiler for mangrove buffers in the Philippines rates flood impacts as decreased [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts], and a second-hand reading of an economic model for coastal districts of northern Vietnam reports that restoration scenarios have even higher cost-benefit ratios when the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is included [ev_frmg_erw09_2].
mangrove_restoration__flood__all__income.conditionality: Neither unit measures flood levels or wave reduction behind a planted stand: the Philippine unit is a compiler rating and the Vietnam unit a model result cited second-hand [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts, ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The Vietnam value is the avoided upkeep of a public sea dike, a saving to society rather than income reaching the households working the coast [ev_frmg_erw09_2].

mangrove_restoration__flood_hazard.mechanism: Compilers for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and mangrove buffers in the Philippines rate flood impacts as decreased, the Bangladesh compiler only slightly [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts]. Of the mangrove restoration projects reviewed globally, 50% state that the habitat provides improved protection from storm events [ev_frmg_nara16_5], and a second-hand reading of an economic model for coastal districts of northern Vietnam reports that restoration scenarios have even higher cost-benefit ratios when the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is included [ev_frmg_erw09_2].
mangrove_restoration__flood_hazard.conditionality: No unit here measures how far a planted stand lowers flood water or waves. The WOCAT entries are compiler ratings; the 50% counts projects that report a benefit, self-reported rather than measured; and the Vietnam dike-cost result is a model read second-hand from the original study, which the citing author does not describe further [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The protection these units describe falls on the coast and the sea dike behind the stand - avoided storm damage and avoided dike maintenance that accrue to society at large, not income for the household that plants or tends the mangroves [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].

mangrove_restoration__flood_hazard__inco.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the row holds two units: the compiler for mangrove buffers in the Philippines rates flood impacts as decreased [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts], and a second-hand reading of an economic model for coastal districts of northern Vietnam reports that restoration scenarios have even higher cost-benefit ratios when the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is included [ev_frmg_erw09_2].
mangrove_restoration__flood_hazard__inco.conditionality: Neither unit measures flood levels or wave reduction behind a planted stand: the Philippine unit is a compiler rating and the Vietnam unit a model result cited second-hand [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts, ev_frmg_erw09_2]. The Vietnam value is the avoided upkeep of a public sea dike, a saving to society rather than income reaching the households working the coast [ev_frmg_erw09_2].

mangrove_restoration__production_gap.mechanism: The only evidence is a WOCAT sheet on mangrove regeneration in Senegal whose compiler rates crop production as increased at the top of the WOCAT scale [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1442_2011_crop_production]; the sheet does not state the pathway.
mangrove_restoration__production_gap.conditionality: A single compiler rating, not a measurement, with no stated mechanism linking mangrove regeneration to crop output.

mangrove_restoration__recurrent_cost.mechanism: Recurrent costs are compiler-entered annual maintenance costs for mangrove plantations on WOCAT sheets: 241.07 USD per hectare per year for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and 20.00 for mangrove buffers in the Philippines [ev_project_cost_wocat_4300_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_578_2016_maintenance].
mangrove_restoration__recurrent_cost.conditionality: Both are WOCAT compiler entries converted from local currency and they differ widely; only the Bangladesh figure falls in the lower-middle-income band used for the class, and neither sheet itemises the maintenance tasks.

mangrove_restoration__rural_poverty.mechanism: Mangrove planting reaches people mainly through aquatic products, and the returns on the planting itself are reported as benefit-cost appraisals. In northern Viet Nam mangroves had a positive impact on additional income for coastal communities through an increase in per hectare yield of aquaculture products such as shells and oyster by 209-789 per cent [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1] - value that accrues to the households harvesting them - and the project's cost-benefit analysis gives commune benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits and 28.86 to 104.96 including them [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]. A global meta-analysis of mangrove restoration reports benefit-cost ratios of 10.50 to 6.83 across discount rates when summing benefits by ecosystem service, and 3.36 to 2.19 using the mean total economic benefit [ev_economic_return_su21_1]; a cited study concludes that the benefits of mangrove reforestation projects outweigh their costs [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1]. WOCAT compilers rate food security and self-sufficiency in Senegal and the risk of production failure in Bangladesh as improved, and rate the long-term cost-benefit of both establishment and maintenance in Bangladesh as positive [ev_food_security_wocat_1442_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_4300_2019_risk_of_production_failure, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare, with regional means of 22,039 to 30,330 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. A second-hand reading of an economic model for three coastal districts of northern Vietnam finds mangrove restoration desirable from an economic perspective based solely on the direct benefits of use by local communities [ev_frmg_erw09_1], and on Mexico's Gulf coast the mangrove reforestation investments at both pilot sites had positive net present values at all three discount rates considered [ev_frmg_mxicr_1].
mangrove_restoration__rural_poverty.conditionality: Nothing here observes household income or poverty against a counterfactual: the outcome is reached through proxies - economic return, food security and reported income gains - and the strongest numbers are project appraisals rather than measured welfare. The 209-789 per cent is a yield increase of aquaculture products, not an income change [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1]. The Viet Nam ratios come from an evaluation commissioned by the implementer, model costs and benefits forward, and the higher ratios include ecological benefits the source says had yet to materialise [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]; the meta-analysis pools unpaired benefit and cost samples, mostly from East and Southeast Asian planting projects [ev_economic_return_su21_1]; the Bangladesh livelihood values are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression, not observed income, and come from grey literature [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. The Vietnam model is cited second-hand and described by the citing author as preliminary [ev_frmg_erw09_1]. The Mexico result is the project's own completion report, its benefits projected forward from planting on former cattle pasture rather than observed, with coastal protection and carbon not valued [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. The WOCAT units are compiler ratings, and the review finding is a conclusion cited from another study [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1]. Two cost findings are kept out of the direction because the saving goes to society, not to households: mangrove restoration projects reported a median cost of US$0.1 per square metre (range 0.05–6.43) and an average replacement cost ratio of 5 (95% CI 3.1–6.9) against submerged breakwaters giving the same wave reduction, and depending on the water depth, mangrove projects in Vietnam can be three to five times cheaper than a breakwater [ev_frmg_nara16_3, ev_frmg_nara16_4]. That comparison assumed far lower breakwater construction costs in Vietnam than in Europe or the USA, applies only to small waves, and the authors note such defences are not always cost effective [ev_frmg_nara16_4].

mangrove_restoration__rural_poverty__inc.mechanism: The upper-middle-income units are appraisals of mangrove planting in Viet Nam and Mexico. In northern Viet Nam mangroves had a positive impact on additional income for coastal communities through an increase in per hectare yield of aquaculture products such as shells and oyster by 209-789 per cent, value that accrues to the households harvesting them [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1], and the project's cost-benefit analysis gives commune benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits and 28.86 to 104.96 including them [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]. A second-hand reading of an economic model for three coastal districts of northern Vietnam finds mangrove restoration desirable based solely on the direct benefits of use by local communities [ev_frmg_erw09_1], and on Mexico's Gulf coast the mangrove reforestation investments at both pilot sites had positive net present values at all three discount rates considered [ev_frmg_mxicr_1].
mangrove_restoration__rural_poverty__inc.conditionality: None of these units measures household income or poverty against a counterfactual, and none states how large the poverty effect is: the 209-789 per cent is an aquaculture yield increase, not income [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1]; the Viet Nam ratios come from an implementer-commissioned evaluation and the higher ones include ecological benefits the source says had yet to materialise [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]; the Vietnam model is preliminary and cited second-hand [ev_frmg_erw09_1]; and the Mexico benefits are projected forward in the project's own completion report [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. The finding that mangrove projects in Vietnam can be three to five times cheaper than a breakwater, depending on the water depth, is a saving to society rather than to households and does not set the direction [ev_frmg_nara16_4]; it assumed far lower breakwater construction costs in Vietnam than in Europe or the USA, applies only to small waves, and the authors note such defences are not always cost effective.

mangrove_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.mechanism: On the coast of Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta, project monitoring relayed by an independent evaluation reports that because of the replanted mangroves coastal erosion was reduced by 40 percent in Ca Mau and the length and area of coastline accreting increased by 20 percent [ev_frmg_vnppar_1], and the evaluation mission found that stabilising the beach with mangroves in Soc Trang has turned the coast into an accretion zone, with the re-established mangroves causing hatchlings to return and improving catches using artisanal fishing methods [ev_frmg_vnppar_2]. The Bangladesh WOCAT compiler reports that surface runoff decreased because of canopy coverage and accretion of sediments in the plantation site, a component of erosion risk [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4300_2019_surface_runoff].
mangrove_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.conditionality: The same evaluation shows both sides of planting: in the areas of Bac Lieu the mission visited, the replanted mangroves had largely been washed away and the coast was eroding rapidly, so accretion followed where the mangroves established and erosion continued where they did not [ev_frmg_vnppar_2]. Siting and establishment decide the result. The Ca Mau figures are the project's own before-and-after monitoring with no counterfactual, relayed by evaluators who could not visit Ca Mau, the Soc Trang finding is a visual observation, and the Bangladesh unit is a compiler rating of runoff used as a component proxy [ev_frmg_vnppar_1, ev_frmg_vnppar_2, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4300_2019_surface_runoff]; there is no controlled measurement of erosion under mangrove restoration. The stabilised coast protects the land behind it, while the improved artisanal catch is a gain to the fishing households.

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__flo.mechanism: Mangroves dissipate wave energy, by up to 75% over a few tens of metres, and lower storm-surge water levels by 5 to 50 centimetres per kilometre of width in measurements from south Florida, where a hurricane surge attenuation rate of 9.4 cm/km has also been measured over relatively continuous mangrove forest, slightly lower along a river corridor [ev_frmg_leon17_1], and where a validated model also showed a much smaller inundated area with mangroves during Hurricane Wilma [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_2, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_1, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_5]. A global model estimates that losing current mangroves would flood 28% more people each year, and in India villages behind mangrove belts had fewer storm-surge deaths and lower household losses [ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_10, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_9]; compilers for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh and mangrove buffers in the Philippines rate flood impacts as reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts]. In Bangladesh, a World Bank modelling study finds that mangrove belts in front of coastal embankments cut shear stress at the embankment toe by 7%-16% where belts average 60 m wide and by 45%-72% where they average 477 m, and a cited model finds 500 m mangrove afforestation patches can mitigate surge current velocities by up to 90% [ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_2, ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2]. A meta-analysis of field measurements finds that existing mangroves reduce wave heights by 31% (95% CI: 25–37%) [ev_frmg_nara16_1]. Of mangrove restoration projects reviewed globally, 50% state that the habitat provides improved protection from storm events, and a cited economic model for northern Vietnam gives restoration scenarios higher cost-benefit ratios once the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is counted [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__flo.conditionality: Attenuation of tidal and surge water levels is far weaker than for short waves, up to 2 cm per 100 m and dependent on creeks, and the wind-wave figure comes from small-wave measurements rather than storm conditions [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_2]. Almost all literature units describe existing mangrove forests, with transfer to restored stands assumed, and protection depends on belt width, tree density, species and inundation depth. The measured surge data are from the USA, the global property benefit is smaller than the benefit to people, and the Bangladesh and Philippines units are compiler ratings rather than measurements [ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_2]. The Bangladesh study is modelled grey literature from the World Bank, and it finds mangroves have only a small effect (<4%) on design total water level because the surge dominates, so their benefit there is protection of embankments from erosion and currents rather than lower flood levels [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2]. The wave and surge figures measure what standing mangroves do, not what planting achieves: the wave meta-analysis covers existing habitat, measured under ‘normal’ conditions of low waves, and the Florida surge rates are measurements over existing forest [ev_frmg_nara16_1, ev_frmg_leon17_1]. That a planted stand will deliver the same is assumed, not measured, in these units. The restoration-project share counts projects that report a benefit, self-reported rather than measured, and the Vietnam dike-cost result is a second-hand reading of the model [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__flo.mechanism: Mangrove belts lower coastal flood impact by attenuating waves and, far more weakly, storm-surge water levels as water passes through the forest, with attenuation depending on inundation depth, tree species, density and the presence of creeks [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3]. Observed wave-height attenuation reaches 1.2% per m of mangrove and gravity-wave energy falls by up to 75% over a few tens of metres, while surface wind waves are expected to be reduced by more than 75% over a kilometre of mangroves; tidal and trans-tidal attenuation is two orders of magnitude smaller, up to 2 cm per 100 m [ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_1, ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_2, ev_flood_hazard_gijsman21_3, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_2]. Measured storm-surge peak water level reduction ranges from 5 to 50 centimetres per kilometre of mangrove width, and a hurricane surge attenuation rate of 9.4 cm/km has been measured over relatively continuous mangrove forest in Southern Florida, slightly lower along a river corridor [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_1, ev_frmg_leon17_1], and a validated model put Hurricane Wilma inundation at 4,220 km2 without mangroves against 2,450 km2 with them [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_5]. The consequences for people and property follow: a global flood model finds that if current mangroves were lost, 29% more land, 28% more people and 9% more property would be damaged every year, with benefits broadly consistent across return periods [ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_2, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_3]; in Orissa, India, mangroves reduced the average number of cyclone deaths in villages within 10km of the coast by 69%, and the village protected by mangroves had the lowest storm-surge loss per household [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_10, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_9]. In Bangladesh a cited model finds 500 m afforestation patches can mitigate current velocities up to 90% [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2], and WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh and the Philippines rate flood impacts as decreased [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts]. The avoided damage has also been monetised: in Orissa, mangroves provided house-protection benefits of USD 1218 per hectare of forest in a single super cyclone [ev_economic_return_das11_1], and in Thailand storm protection accounted for US$ 8,966-10,821 per hectare, about 87% of estimated mangrove value, with the long-term total economic value of an intact mangrove swamp about 3.6 times that of converting it to shrimp aquaculture [ev_economic_return_marois15_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_2]. A meta-analysis of field measurements finds that existing mangroves reduce wave heights by 31% (95% CI: 25–37%) [ev_frmg_nara16_1]. Of mangrove restoration projects reviewed globally, 50% state that the habitat provides improved protection from storm events, and a cited economic model for northern Vietnam gives restoration scenarios higher cost-benefit ratios once the avoided maintenance cost of the sea dike system, protected from coastal storm surges by the mangroves, is counted [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__flo.conditionality: The monetised figures are society-wide avoided damage - averted property loss and protection service valued wherever it falls - and not income reaching the rural households a World Bank investment targets, so they say what the hazard protection is worth, not what the practice pays its adopters [ev_economic_return_das11_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_2]. That value does not settle the land-use case: in Orissa the value of coastal land in alternate uses far exceeds the value mangroves provide by protecting residential property, and on that information alone mangrove conservation or rehabilitation could not be justified [ev_economic_return_das11_2]; the same Orissa figure is a single-event amount with no stated price year and is not annualised [ev_economic_return_das11_1], and the Thai values are model estimates cited in a review, the larger of them covering timber, non-timber products and fisheries as well as coastal protection [ev_economic_return_marois15_1, ev_economic_return_marois15_2]. Most of the units here, measured and modelled alike, describe existing mangrove forest rather than restored stands, including the global model, whose counterfactual is the loss of current mangroves rather than new planting, so the step from standing forest to a restoration investment is assumed rather than evidenced [ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_1, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_2, ev_flood_hazard_menendez20_3, ev_economic_return_marois15_1]. Protection is also conditional on width and on what dominates the water level: the Bangladesh study finds mangroves have a small effect (<4%) on total water level because the design level is dominated by the surge, which is unaffected by mangroves in that model [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2]. On evidence quality, the measured surge reductions all come from south Florida in the USA, the wind-wave reduction is derived from small-wave rather than storm measurements, the Orissa household-loss comparison is a perception-based survey of a handful of villages, much of the review material is cited secondary rather than new measurement, and the WOCAT entries are compiler ratings [ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_1, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_2, ev_frmg_leon17_1, ev_flood_hazard_mcivor12_9, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_578_2016_flood_impacts]. The wave and surge figures measure what standing mangroves do, not what planting achieves: the wave meta-analysis covers existing habitat, measured under ‘normal’ conditions of low waves, and the Florida surge rates are measurements over existing forest [ev_frmg_nara16_1, ev_frmg_leon17_1]. That a planted stand will deliver the same is assumed, not measured, in these units. The restoration-project share counts projects that report a benefit, self-reported rather than measured, and the Vietnam dike-cost result is a second-hand reading of the model [ev_frmg_nara16_5, ev_frmg_erw09_2].

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__rur.mechanism: What is left in this row is evidence on costs and on benefits that reach people: mangrove planting supports coastal livelihoods mainly through aquatic products, and the returns on the planting itself are reported as benefit-cost ratings. In northern Viet Nam a community mangrove plantation raised per-hectare yields of aquaculture products such as shells and oysters by 209-789 per cent, providing additional income for coastal communities [ev_household_income_ifrc11_1], and the project's cost-benefit analysis gives commune benefit-cost ratios of 3.06 to 68.92 excluding ecological benefits and 28.86 to 104.96 including them [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]. A global meta-analysis of mangrove restoration reports a benefit-cost ratio of 3.36 to 2.19 across discount rates when using the mean value of estimated total economic benefits [ev_economic_return_su21_1], a cited study concludes that the benefits of mangrove reforestation projects outweigh their costs [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1], and in Orissa, India, a comparison of costs and benefits found protecting the remaining mangroves economically justified against the forgone agricultural land [ev_economic_return_dasvincent09_1]. WOCAT compilers rate food security and self-sufficiency in Senegal and the risk of production failure in Bangladesh as improved, and rate the long-term cost-benefit of both establishment and maintenance as positive [ev_food_security_wocat_1442_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_4300_2019_risk_of_production_failure, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_maintenance_long]. A World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD/ha, with regional means of 22,039 to 30,330 USD/ha [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. Two mangrove appraisals point the same way: a second-hand reading of an economic model for three coastal districts of northern Vietnam finds mangrove restoration desirable from an economic perspective based solely on the direct benefits of use by local communities [ev_frmg_erw09_1], and in Mexico's Gulf coast the mangrove reforestation investments at both pilot sites had positive net present values at all three discount rates considered [ev_frmg_mxicr_1].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__rur.conditionality: Monetised avoided storm damage no longer sits in this row: it is hazard protection whose value accrues to society at large rather than income reaching the targeted households, and it is accounted under coastal flood hazard instead. What remains is thin on direct measurement of poverty. Nothing here observes household income or poverty against a counterfactual: the outcome is reached only through proxies - economic return, food security and reported income gains - and the strongest cost-benefit numbers are project appraisals rather than measured welfare [ev_economic_return_su21_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_household_income_ifrc11_1]. The Viet Nam figures come from an evaluation commissioned by the implementer, model costs and benefits forward, and the higher ratios include ecological benefits the source says had yet to materialise [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_ifrc11_2]; the meta-analysis pools unpaired benefit and cost samples and is dominated by East and Southeast Asian planting projects [ev_economic_return_su21_1]; the Bangladesh livelihood values are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression, not observed income, and come from grey literature with the positive bias that carries [ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. The Orissa comparison concerns retaining existing mangroves rather than restoring new ones, and its own quote notes that the government's early warning evidently saved more lives than mangroves did [ev_economic_return_dasvincent09_1]. Several of the units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than measurements, and the review finding is a conclusion cited from another study rather than a result of its own [ev_food_security_wocat_1442_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_4300_2019_risk_of_production_failure, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4300_2019_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1]. The Vietnam model is cited second-hand and described by the citing author as preliminary [ev_frmg_erw09_1]. The Mexico result is the project's own completion report, and its benefits are projected forward from planting on former cattle pasture rather than observed; coastal protection and carbon were not valued [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. Two cost findings are kept out of the direction because the saving goes to society rather than to households: mangrove restoration projects reported a median cost of US$0.1 per square metre (range 0.05–6.43) and an average replacement cost ratio of 5 (95% CI 3.1–6.9) against submerged breakwaters giving the same wave reduction, and depending on the water depth, mangrove projects in Vietnam can be three to five times cheaper than a breakwater [ev_frmg_nara16_3, ev_frmg_nara16_4]. That comparison assumed far lower breakwater construction costs in Vietnam than in Europe or the USA, rests on wave reduction measured under normal low-wave conditions, applies only to small waves, and the authors note such defences are not always cost effective.

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__soi.mechanism: On the coast of Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta, project monitoring relayed by an independent evaluation reports that because of the replanted mangroves coastal erosion was reduced by 40 percent in Ca Mau and the length and area of coastline accreting increased by 20 percent, and the evaluation mission found that stabilising the beach with mangroves in Soc Trang has turned the coast into an accretion zone [ev_frmg_vnppar_1, ev_frmg_vnppar_2]. The Bangladesh WOCAT compiler reports that surface runoff decreased because of canopy cover and sediment accretion in the mangrove plantation, a component of erosion risk. A World Bank modelling study for Bangladesh finds mangrove belts reduce shear stress at the toe of coastal embankments by 7%-16% where they average 60 m wide and by 45%-72% where they average 477 m, which also allows thinner revetments [ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_2].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__soi.conditionality: Apart from the Vietnam project's own uncontrolled monitoring, relayed by evaluators who could not visit Ca Mau, and the mission's visual observation in Soc Trang [ev_frmg_vnppar_1, ev_frmg_vnppar_2], the pool is one compiler rating of runoff used as a component proxy and modelled shear-stress reductions at embankments from grey literature [ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wbmang25_2]; there is no controlled measurement of erosion under mangrove restoration. The Vietnam evidence also separates standing mangroves from planting: in the areas of Bac Lieu the mission visited, the replanted mangroves had largely been washed away and the coast was eroding rapidly, so accretion followed where the mangroves established and erosion continued where they did not [ev_frmg_vnppar_2].

mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__win.mechanism: Mangrove planting in northern Viet Nam is credited with keeping a sea dyke undamaged in a 2005 typhoon of the same level as one that damaged it in 1987, and with cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent; planted Sonneratia mangroves in Hainan, China cut mean wind speed behind the stand by 59.4% during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. A global model credits current mangroves with reducing flood damages from tropical cyclones, and compilers for mangrove buffers in the Philippines and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_menendez20_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_578_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Studies of standing mangroves show the protection that keeping the forest provides. In Orissa, India, villages with wider mangroves between them and the coast had significantly fewer deaths in the 1999 super cyclone, with 1.72 additional deaths per village within 10 km of the coast predicted had mangrove width been reduced to zero [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_2], and without mangroves the area would have seen 23% more fully collapsed houses [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_das11_1]. In Central America category 3 hurricane winds would lead to a 24% decrease in economic activity where mangrove width was less than 1 km but no damage where it was wider [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_delvalle20_1], and across coastal communities direct cyclone exposure cost 5.4–6.7 months of economic activity at average mangrove extent against 2.6–5.5 months with more extensive mangroves [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_hochard19_1]. Numerical models and laboratory experiments support mangroves reducing the water height and velocity of cyclone storm surges, a South Florida model concluded a 7–8 km wide mangrove forest could reduce a category 3 hurricane's surges by ~80%, and in Belize cleared sites lost significantly more field equipment in storms than sites with intact mangrove [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_3, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_4]. An independent World Bank evaluation in Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta draws the lesson that where reforestation was successful, land is accreting and farming and other economic activities are protected from storms, wind, and salt [ev_frmg_vnppar_8].
mangrove_restoration__tidal_coastal__win.conditionality: The Viet Nam results are uncontrolled before-and-after comparisons attributed to mangroves by evaluators of the implementing Red Cross programme, and the global model concerns existing rather than restored mangroves [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_menendez20_1]. The Philippines and Bangladesh units are compiler ratings, not measurements, and the Bangladesh compiler rates only a slight reduction [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Protection weakens where the surge is largest: in Orissa the death-reducing effect was smaller for above-mean storm surges [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_dasvincent09_3], and no mangrove effect on fully collapsed houses was visible within 10 km of the coast, where many houses were swept away instead [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_das11_2]. A review finds that observational studies have not given conclusive results on how much protection mangroves provide [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_2]. The Orissa, Central American and global community studies are quasi-experimental comparisons of places with more or less existing mangrove, so they measure the service of keeping mangroves rather than the performance of planted stands, and the Florida surge figure is a model result cited in a review [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_marois15_3]. That lesson is the evaluator's synthesis of field findings, not a measurement, and the same passage records the reverse where mangrove seedlings were planted too small, at too shallow a depth and not carefully monitored: there the coastline is moving inland, endangering the dikes built to protect the resettled areas [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. The contrast separates what standing mangroves do from what planting achieves: the Orissa, Central American and global comparisons measure existing forest, while the Vietnam evaluation found farming protected where the planting succeeded and the coastline moving inland where the seedlings failed.

mangrove_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.mechanism: Planted mangroves are credited with sheltering the coast and what lies behind it from typhoons. In northern Viet Nam a storm in 1987 caused serious damage to a three km-stretch of sea-dyke that cost 300,000 US dollars to repair, while during the 2005 storm the same dyke did not sustain any damage, which the evaluation attributes to the protective capacity of the mangrove forests [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1]; damage to private property fell further, from 90 per cent of shrimp farm value destroyed in 1996 to 25 per cent ten years later [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]. Behind planted Sonneratia mangroves in Hainan, China, mean and extreme wind speed during typhoons were reduced by 59.4% and 53.2% [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. Compilers for mangrove buffers in the Philippines and mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as decreased [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_578_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. An independent World Bank evaluation in Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta draws the lesson that where reforestation was successful, land is accreting and farming and other economic activities are protected from storms, wind, and salt [ev_frmg_vnppar_8].
mangrove_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.conditionality: Who benefits differs by unit: the sea-dyke saving is a public asset protected for the coast behind the stand, while the shrimp-farm figure is damage avoided on private property [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2]. The Viet Nam results are before-and-after comparisons between storms with no control site, attributed to the mangroves by evaluators of the implementing Red Cross programme, and the Hainan figure is a secondary citation [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. The Philippines and Bangladesh units are compiler ratings, not measurements, and the Bangladesh compiler rates only a slight reduction [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. The Mekong Delta lesson is the evaluator's synthesis of field findings, not a measurement, and the same passage records the reverse where mangrove seedlings were planted too small, at too shallow a depth and not carefully monitored: there the coastline is moving inland, sweeping away solid ground and endangering the dikes built to protect the resettled areas [ev_frmg_vnppar_8]. Siting and establishment are the hinge: the protection reported here follows where the planting took hold, and the same coast lost ground where it did not.
